key_insight: DMuon makes matrix-orthogonalization training practical at scale by cutting Muon’s optimizer overhead to near-AdamW levels without requiring framework changes.
engineering_relevance: It provides a drop-in distributed optimizer path for large-model training systems where standard element-wise optimizer assumptions make vanilla Muon too slow.
method: Integrates Muon as an open-source distributed module for existing training pipelines.
Accelerates matrix-level updates, including costly Newton-Schulz iterations.
Targets end-to-end step-time reduction while preserving Muon’s convergence benefits.
evidence_signal: Across embodied foundation model and LLM workloads, the abstract reports 1.48x-3.01x faster end-to-end steps and 6.85x-163.00x faster optimizer steps versus baseline Muon.
watch_item: Reported gains depend on implementation and workload characteristics, so the distributed overhead and compatibility with different model shapes should be validated in each deployment.
paper_title: DMuon: Efficient Distributed Muon Training with Near-Adam Overhead
